fixes.explanation: Not this time, baker, because that statement is true. The writer says "the One who was born of God protects him, and the evil one cannot touch him." (1 John 5:18) Notice who does the protecting: the One who was born of God, not the person himself. That's a lot of weight to put on a single verse, and it holds.

I can see why you'd think that, friend, but authority isn't the gift named here. The Son of God "…has given us understanding, so that we may know Him who is true…" (1 John 5:20) The understanding comes with a purpose, and the purpose is knowing Him. The verse then says we are in Him who is true, in His Son Jesus Christ.

I see why you'd pick that, baker, but strong drink isn't named in this verse. Right before it, the writer says of Jesus Christ, "He is the true God and eternal life." (1 John 5:20) Then comes the closing line, "Little children, keep yourselves from idols." (1 John 5:21) So the letter ends by pointing from the true God to idols.
